jobs.title: Program Director, Catalytic Deployment
jobs.description:
About OpenAI Foundation

AI is already changing how people work, learn, and access care. It has the potential to unlock extraordinary benefits—faster medical breakthroughs, accelerated scientific discovery, more personalized services in healthcare and education, new tools for creativity and invention, higher productivity and economic growth, improved public services like transportation systems, and so much more.

But building powerful systems to benefit humanity is only a part of the work of our mission. Advanced AI models will also present new challenges that are already surfacing, and we need to be prepared to identify these challenges and develop solutions to address them.

These are the two dimensions of what we’re building the Foundation to do. We aim to enable the use of AI to find solutions to humanity’s hardest problems, transform what people are capable of, and deliver real benefits in people’s lives—while working hard with partners to be ready for new challenges, and to help make society resilient, as AI advances.

This work is just beginning. Over the next year, as we quickly ramp up, the Foundation expects to invest at least $1 billion across life sciences and curing diseases, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs. This includes early investments toward our previously announced $25 billion commitment to curing diseases and AI resilience.

About Civil Society And Philanthropy

Civil Society and Philanthropy is a new OpenAI Foundation team dedicated to putting advanced AI to work on challenges facing people and communities globally.

We will partner with nonprofit and civil society organizations and governments around the world, putting in place the resources needed to ensure AI can meaningfully support their work. We combine philanthropic investment, technical expertise, and convening power to work alongside trusted partners that deliver essential services across geographies and issue areas. Together, we identify opportunities where AI can strengthen their work, expand their reach, and tangibly benefit their communities.

We're starting with three areas:

Put AI to work in essential services where it can meaningfully improve access and outcomes.
Give civil society organizations the tools, expertise, and support to adopt AI responsibly.
Build shared infrastructure so that successful tools and lessons can benefit the entire social sector.

We believe the most meaningful applications of AI will be shaped not by technology companies alone, but by the teachers, clinicians, legal advocates, public servants, researchers, governments, and community organizations applying these tools to solve real-world problems.

About The Role

The Program Director is a leadership role on the Catalytic Deployments team that combines philanthropic investment, strategy, institution-building, and operations. Catalytic Deployments is a small, flat, and fast-moving team designed to make large and transformative investments across a wide range of areas in civil society.

Program Directors own the strategy and execution of major areas of the Catalytic Deployments portfolio, working closely with the Head of Catalytic Deployments to set overall team priorities. As part of this work, Program Directors will help lead the development of large philanthropic investments globally, from grants to ambitious multi-year initiatives, and potentially new institutions. Program Directors will be part of a small, collaborative team and expected to work closely with the rest of the organization.

Ideal program directors have deep experience in at least one social sector domain, such as public health, education, poverty alleviation, and economic mobility.

This role requires strong judgment, high ownership, and the ability to operate with meaningful autonomy. This role has an unusually high bar for judgment, strategic thinking, and execution velocity.

In the first year, Program Directors will develop a clear investment thesis in one or more priority domains; build a high-quality pipeline of opportunities; launch several significant partnerships or investments; and help establish the operating model and team for Catalytic Deployments.

This role reports to the Head of Catalytic Deployments, Civil Society and Philanthropy.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We currently use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. Some travel around the U.S. and to other countries will be required.

In this role, you will:

Contribute to the strategy, prioritization, and the Foundation’s approach to Catalytic Deployments; over time, own specific areas within Catalytic Deployments
Source, evaluate, and recommend grants and other funding opportunities. Conduct diligence on organizations, projects, and leaders, including execution capability and potential for scaling the benefit of AI-enabled approaches
Help design and manage a growing portfolio of grants, ensuring strong judgment, clear prioritization, and high-quality follow-through
As the organization grows, manage other members of the Catalytic Deployments team
Engage deeply with the external ecosystem, including researchers, nonprofits, academic centers, public-interest organizations, data platforms, funders, and other potential grantee organizations
Identify gaps in the current ecosystem and develop ideas for how the Foundation can support new efforts, partnerships, or field-building initiatives
Develop and launch new initiatives from zero-to-one, including helping shape concepts, convene stakeholders, and stand up new efforts where needed
Represent the Foundation in external conversations, helping to build credibility, source opportunities, and strengthen the broader field
Write clear internal recommendations and strategy memos to support decision-making
Use frontier AI to support your work across the activities described above

You might thrive in this role if you:

10+ years of leadership experience in nonprofits, philanthropy, or government
Credible experience building and scaling large social-sector initiatives
Experience in sourcing, assessing, and structuring grants
Subject matter expertise in at least one social sector domain, such as public health, education, poverty alleviation, and economic mobility
Ability to reason clearly about AI capabilities, implementation constraints, organizational readiness and the risks of deploying AI systems in civil society contexts. (Strongly preferred: Direct experience deploying or scaling AI-enabled approaches in at least one social-sector domain. Demonstrated out-of-the-box and original thinking about AI-for-good.)
Demonstrated ability to evaluate technical or organizational opportunities and make strong recommendations
Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities may evolve over time
Experience engaging credibly with external experts, institutions, and senior stakeholders
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information clearly and persuasively
Strong strategic judgment combined with a bias toward execution
High degree of ownership, discretion, and accountability
Deep motivation to accelerate AI’s impact in civil society and contribute to the Foundation’s mission

Compensation

The annual base salary range for this role is $270,000 to $330,000 USD.

This range reflects our good-faith estimate of the base salary we reasonably expect to pay for this position upon hire. Actual base salary will be determined based on job-related factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, skills, expertise, the scope of the role, and work location, as applicable.

This salary range does not include benefits or any other compensation for which the role may be eligible.

Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the School of Humanities and Sciences Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring freeze.

Work Arrangement:
This is a hybrid position with 3-4 days per week onsite. May require working flexible hours, including occasional work on evenings and weekends.

Budgeted Salary:
The budgeted salary range for this position is $251,322 – $276,576 per annum.

Department/Program Description

The School of Humanities and Sciences is Stanford's largest school and home to the majority of Stanford undergraduates, to a significant number of graduate students, and to foundational research across the arts, humanities, natural sciences, and social sciences. With 24 departments and 25 interdisciplinary programs, H&S fuels world-class teaching, learning, and research on questions ranging from artificial intelligence and democracy to climate, public health, philosophy, and the arts. Led by Dean Debra Satz, the school is dedicated to ensuring that every Stanford student, regardless of major, engages meaningfully with the humanities, arts, and sciences, and that the school's research and ideas reach and inform audiences far beyond campus.

For more information on the school, click here .

Brief Position Summary

The School of Humanities and Sciences seeks an experienced, dynamic communicator, skilled manager, and team-builder to serve as our Chief Communications Officer. Reporting to the Associate Dean for External Relations, who also serves as Stanford’s Associate Vice President for Development in the Office of Development, with a dotted line to the Dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences, the person in this role will manage a nimble team of communications professionals and oversee all communications strategies and activities, including executive and internal communications; media relations and issues management; marketing communications; digital strategy and social media; news, storytelling, and content creation; and brand management.

In addition to working closely with the H&S Dean and the Associate Dean for External Relations, this position will collaborate with the school’s senior associate deans, department chairs, faculty, and staff, as well as colleagues from University Communications and other key partners across campus, to coordinate strategies and activities and to leverage resources to maximize communications impact for the school.

While the current team consists of two professional communicators, we anticipate making resources available to grow and build the team over time to carry out the communications activities of the school.

The successful candidate will be a strategic thinker and a talented writer and editor who will bring to the position a collaborative leadership style, a sophisticated understanding of communications and messaging across a wide range of disciplines and audiences, and demonstrated experience working within a large, complex organization.

In This Role You Will

Develop and implement a strategic communications plan that addresses all stakeholders and continues to build the school's reputation and visibility on a global level throughmessaging for multiple audiences, promotion of research activities via media outreach and external engagement, a best-in-class digital presence, a robust internal communications and employee engagement program, and oversight of the school brand.
Provide strategic communications advice to school leadership, faculty, and staff, including working with the Dean to help create and disseminate executive communications, such as speeches, talking points, and messaging.
Serve as the school's primary spokesperson and direct crisis communications for emergency matters and issues with reputational impact across the school's 24 departments and 25 interdisciplinary programs.
Devise and implement creative, compelling, and effective means of communicating the breadth and depth of faculty research, student opportunities, alumni impact, academic excellence, and the essential nature of the school and its many disciplines.
Oversee key school messages and develop strategies for multiple audiences, channels, and constituencies, including faculty, students, alumni, university leadership, and the public.
Manage the H&S brand to ensure consistency and accuracy in alignment with university brand and name-use guidelines.
Direct the management and operations of public-facing communications programs, platforms, and channels—including media relations, the school website, social media, and email newsletters—to ensure strategic implementation, efficiency, and consistency with school branding and priorities.
In collaboration with University Communications, define and execute a proactive media relations strategy that establishes the Dean, faculty leaders, and H&S as thought leaders across the humanities, arts, and sciences.
Hire, manage, mentor, and retain a staff of professionals; engage outside contractors as needed; and manage the team's annual budget.
Collaborate with University Communications and school leadership to align communication strategy and activities; support alignment within the school's departments, programs, and units; and establish communication and brand guidelines and best practices to help colleagues achieve goals.
Perform other duties as assigned.

This is a 100% FTE, continuing, exempt position.

If you believe that this opportunity is a match for your knowledge, skills, and abilities, we encourage you to apply.

A resume and cover letter are required for consideration.

Thank you for considering employment opportunities with the School of Humanities and Sciences.

Experience with Microsoft Office, Google Drive, Zoom, and standard office equipment.

About Us

Circle is building the world’s leading AI-powered, all-in-one platform for digital businesses. We make it possible for creators, coaches, educators, and businesses to bring together their audience with engaging discussions, live streams, events, chat, courses, and payments — all in one place, all under their own brand.

We’re proud to be a fully remote company of around 270 (and growing!) team members from 30+ countries around the world. We seek exceptional individuals around the world, set them up to do the best work of their lives, and in turn, create a meaningful impact in their own lives. We don't track hours, but we do manage for high expectations very closely. We collaborate across time zones, are highly async, and like to document a lot.

Twice a year, we bring the whole company together in beautiful places around the world for our company offsites. So far, we’ve hosted offsites in Turkey, Portugal, Mexico, Thailand, Colombia, Italy, Ireland, and more, with still more to come!

Check out our Careers
page for more about working at Circle.

About The Role

The Director of Strategic Partnerships will lead the strategy, growth, and performance of Circle's partnerships function, building programs and relationships that strengthen Circle's brand while driving meaningful business outcomes.

This role sits at the intersection of business development, partnerships, creators, content, and growth. You'll be responsible for translating Circle's broader company priorities into a forward-looking partnerships strategy, identifying where and how we invest, developing our most important creator and strategic relationships, and ensuring those investments translate into measurable impact across customer growth, brand awareness, and market position.

A core part of the role is bringing strong creative and commercial judgment to the work, operating as a genuine strategic partner to the people on the other side of the table. You'll cultivate and maintain those relationships directly, building campaigns, offers, content, and experiences that feel authentic to their audiences — and developing strategies that grow revenue for both parties, so that Circle and the partner each achieve their own goals rather than just executing against Circle's priorities.

You'll also build the systems, team, and operating model required to scale the function, moving successful initiatives from one-off execution into repeatable programs that can grow without depending on a single person to drive every detail. This is essential to the function’s ability to achieve significant impact on ICP trials and for the director to be successful in this role. In addition to the operational expertise to move something from incubation to repeatable system, this role has to also be creative enough to continuously develop new strategic programs.

Reporting to our SVP, Ecosystem, you'll work closely with Circle's founders and leadership team, as well as teammates across Community Growth, Media, Demand Generation, Product Marketing, our Design Studio.

What You'll Be Doing

Own Circle's Partnerships strategic planning, and roadmap, using deep, company-wide knowledge of Circle's business, strategy, and goals to originate new concepts and ideas that extend the function's impact beyond its current scope — connecting partnership investments to company priorities, measurable business outcomes, and providing strategic direction to managers across multiple areas and operations.
Take ownership of the function's contribution to new business and other agreed performance goals, using those outcomes to inform where we invest, what we build, and how we prioritize.

Accrediting Commission of Career Schools and Colleges (ACCSC)

Lead the Future of Accreditation. Champion Student Success.

The Accrediting Commission of Career Schools and Colleges (ACCSC) is seeking an accomplished, visionary, and mission-driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer.

As the chief executive and administrative officer of ACCSC, the Executive Director will work closely with the Commission, Chair, and Executive Committee to advance the organization's mission, ensure the integrity and effectiveness of the accreditation process, and position ACCSC as a respected and forward-thinking authority in career education.

For nearly six decades, ACCSC has been dedicated to promoting educational quality and accountability in career-focused institutions, helping ensure that students receive the training and education necessary to achieve meaningful workforce success. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to shape the future of accreditation while advancing innovation, accountability, and student achievement.

Key Responsibilities

The Executive Director will:
Assist and support the Commission in achieving its mission of serving as a dependable authority as to the quality of education and training offered by career education institutions.
Assist and support the Commission in establishing and fostering high educational standards, quality, accountability, and ethical practices among accredited institutions.
Administer the Commission’s operations including but not limited to all aspects of the accreditation process, annual budgets and financial management, organizational design and IT infrastructure, staff management and human resources, and physical space and equipment.
Cultivate and distribute timely information, advice, and direction needed by the Commission to set strategy; develop accrediting standards, policies, procedures; and make accreditation decision
Ensure the delivery of clear and timely correspondence to member institutions expressing the Commission’s decisions, actions, and guidance as well as any changes or revisions to the Standards of Accreditation or the accreditation process.
Implement actions determined by the Commission and perform such other duties as assigned by the Chair of ACCSC, Executive Committee, or the Commission.
Maintain effective and harmonious relationships with the Commission, staff, the U.S. Department of Education, state regulators, accredited institutions, other accrediting agencies, trade associations representing career schools, and other ACCSC constituents.
Engage in education policy discussions across a spectrum of forums representing the interests of ACCSC and accreditation as an enterprise.
Schedule, plan, and attend all meetings of the Commission and the Executive Committee participating in deliberations in a non-voting capacity unless otherwise directed by the Executive Committee.
Devote time and attention to professional development activities, scholarships, and research that are complementary to ACCSC.

The Executive Director is accountable to the Commission for the successful achievement of these duties and responsibilities, with the Chair acting on behalf of the Commission to oversee and review the Executive Director’s annual performance in accordance with the administrative policies and procedures of ACCSC.

Qualifications and Experience:

Successful candidates will have significant senior leadership experience (i.e., 10+ years) in one or more of the following areas:
Institutional or programmatic accreditation
Higher education administration
Education policy
Regulatory compliance
Nonprofit governance

The strongest candidates may come from backgrounds such as:
Senior executive leadership within an accrediting agency
President or CEO of an education-focused nonprofit organization
Senior higher education administration
Education policy leadership
Chief academic or compliance officer roles within multi-campus educational systems

Experience working with the U.S. Department of Education, accreditation recognition processes, Title IV issues, compliance oversight, and regulatory environments is highly desirable.

Leadership Characteristics

Commitment to student-centered decision-making
Strong belief in accountability, peer review, and continuous improvement
Strategic thinking and sound judgment
Exceptional communication skills
Integrity, transparency, and professionalism
The ability to lead effectively in complex regulatory environments
A collaborative leadership style and strong governance partnership skills

Education

A graduate degree in a field aligned to the requirements and expectations of the position such as educational or organizational leadership, educational administration, public policy, nonprofit management, is required.
A doctorate or terminal professional degree (e.g., Ph.D., Ed.D., J.D.) is strongly preferred.

We are seeking an experienced, visionary, and deeply relational Chief Executive Officer

The next CEO will lead an established organization with a strong community reputation, committed staff, engaged volunteers, and a clear mission, while also helping shape the future of the organization.

To enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible citizens.

The ideal candidate will be both strategic and hands-on

The CEO will provide overall leadership for BGCWC's programs, people, operations, finances, fundraising, partnerships, and community presence. Key areas of responsibility include:

About INSPIRE Alliance

INSPIRE Alliance is a Texas nonprofit corporation established by the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station (TEES) with support from The Texas A&M University System Board of Regents. The Alliance was created to advance leadership in applied national security research by accelerating the development and deployment of mission-ready engineering solutions.

As a 501(c)(3) organization, INSPIRE Alliance provides a flexible platform for pursuing contracts, grants and strategic partnerships in the national security sector. Working across government, academia and industry, the Alliance is designed to rapidly translate research and innovation into real-world capabilities that strengthen security, resilience and operational effectiveness.

INSPIRE Alliance focuses on critical technology areas including autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, space innovation, data science and advanced materials. Its mission is to serve as a trusted agent for engineering solutions while expanding research impact, strengthening strategic partnerships and advancing national security priorities.

Position Summary

INSPIRE Alliance is seeking a President & Chief Executive Officer to serve as the organization's principal executive leader and guide its next phase of development and growth.

The CEO will be responsible for transforming an emerging organizational platform into a mature, high-performing national security research and innovation enterprise. This executive will establish the strategic direction, operating capability, sponsor relationships, talent and infrastructure necessary to scale the Alliance while preserving the speed, flexibility and mission focus that distinguish its operating model.

Operating at the intersection of national security, federal contracting, institutional governance and academic research, the CEO must be equally credible in defense and university environments. The successful candidate will understand the urgency and acquisition priorities of federal sponsors while effectively navigating the governance, research and administrative structures of a university-affiliated organization.

Working closely with the Board of Directors and executive leadership, the CEO will position INSPIRE Alliance as a premier partner for federal agencies, military organizations, academic institutions and industry seeking mission-ready research, engineering and technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, Growth and Organizational Scale
Establish and execute a long-term strategic vision aligned with the INSPIRE Alliance mission, Department of War priorities and national security objectives.
Build the organizational capabilities required to scale from an emerging enterprise into a mature, sustainable and high-output operating organization.
Translate strategic priorities into measurable goals, performance indicators and accountable execution plans.
Identify opportunities for program expansion, new capabilities and strategic investment while maintaining disciplined focus on mission impact.
Sustain a high-energy, project-driven operating culture that values speed, sound judgment and execution without sacrificing quality or compliance.

Federal Growth and Sponsor Development
Develop and expand relationships with senior leaders across the Department of War, military services, federal agencies, service laboratories, program executive offices (PEOs) and other national security organizations.
Position INSPIRE Alliance for competitive federal opportunities, including prime contract roles, strategic teaming arrangements and consortium-based partnerships.
Apply strong knowledge of federal acquisition and contracting pathways, including Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) vehicles and Other Transaction Authority/Agreement (OTA) mechanisms.
Lead organizational revenue growth through federal contracts, grants, sponsorships, partnerships and other diversified funding sources in coordination with the Director of Business Development.
Build sustained sponsor relationships by understanding mission requirements, anticipating emerging priorities and ensuring INSPIRE Alliance delivers measurable value.

Organizational Leadership and Operations
Provide executive oversight of programs, finance, compliance, human capital, infrastructure and organizational administration.
Recruit, develop and retain high-performing leaders and teams capable of operating effectively in a complex national security environment.
Establish scalable business processes, management systems and secure operating practices that support growth across a substantial sponsored portfolio.
Monitor organizational performance, resolve barriers to execution and continuously strengthen operational effectiveness.
Foster a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, integrity and disciplined decision-making.

Governance, Financial Stewardship and Risk
Serve as the principal executive liaison to the Board of Directors, providing timely, transparent and strategic information necessary for effective governance and decision-making.
Execute Board-approved policies, initiatives and organizational priorities.
Maintain strong financial stewardship through disciplined budgeting, resource allocation, forecasting and executive-level financial reporting.
Establish and maintain effective governance, compliance and enterprise risk management practices appropriate for a national security-focused nonprofit organization.
Ensure disciplined management of security-sensitive requirements, including ITAR, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements and classified information handling as applicable.
Exercise sound executive judgment in evaluating opportunities, including declining work when compliance, security or institutional risk outweighs strategic value.

External Leadership and Strategic Partnerships
Serve as the principal ambassador for INSPIRE Alliance with government, military, university, industry and community stakeholders.
Build productive relationships across The Texas A&M University System, faculty, research leadership and academic administration while protecting the Alliance's ability to operate with appropriate speed and flexibility.
Communicate effectively with senior military leaders, government executives, industry partners, researchers and institutional leaders, translating priorities across defense and academic environments.
Strengthen collaboration among academia, government and industry to accelerate the transition of research and technology into operational capability.
Represent INSPIRE Alliance at executive meetings, industry forums, sponsor engagements and other external events.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business administration, public policy, higher education, nonprofit management or a related field.
Master's degree in business administration, public administration, organizational leadership or a related field.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience in national security, nonprofit leadership, higher education, applied research, research alliances or another mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated success building or scaling organizations, programs or business units through significant periods of growth and increasing operational complexity.
Proven record of developing federal sponsor relationships and securing substantial funding through contracts, grants, partnerships, sponsorships or other revenue sources.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across government, academia and industry, including the ability to reconcile differing institutional cultures, priorities and decision-making processes.
Strong understanding of federal acquisition, contracting and sponsored research environments.
Executive-level financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation and Board-level financial reporting.
Experience establishing effective governance, compliance, security and risk management practices.
Demonstrated success leading senior teams and developing high-performing organizations.
Exceptional executive communication, relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to make sound decisions in complex, ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.
Demonstrated integrity, discretion and sound judgment in matters involving sensitive information, institutional risk and public trust.
Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications
Active U.S. government security clearance.
Significant experience supporting Department of War programs, federal contracts, military acquisition organizations or national security initiatives.
Established relationships across federal defense organizations, military services, program executive offices, laboratories or related sponsor communities.
Experience leading a university-affiliated applied research organization, national security nonprofit, federal research enterprise, defense-focused business or similar organization.
Direct experience with IDIQs, OTAs, consortium structures and other federal acquisition pathways.
Experience managing ITAR, CUI, CMMC, classified programs or comparable national security compliance requirements.
Prior military service, particularly experience as a commissioned officer, commander or acquisition leader.

Executive Leadership Profile

The successful CEO will be a builder rather than a caretaker. INSPIRE Alliance requires an executive capable of strengthening the organization's operating foundation while aggressively pursuing the relationships, capabilities and opportunities necessary for long-term scale.

This leader must be fluent in both the language of national security and the culture of academic research. The CEO must understand mission capability, sponsor urgency and acquisition priorities while maintaining credibility with faculty, researchers and university leadership.

Equally important is a sustained bias toward execution. The CEO must be comfortable absorbing complexity, making decisions and maintaining organizational momentum in a fast-moving environment. Growth must be achieved without diluting the Alliance's strategic purpose, compromising compliance or allowing unnecessary administrative complexity to erode its speed advantage.

Additional Requirements

The position requires regular engagement with federal, military, academic and industry partners and may involve significant travel. The CEO must be comfortable operating in sensitive, confidential and classified-adjacent environments and must demonstrate an unwavering commitment to compliance, accountability, ethical leadership and responsible stewardship of public trust.

To Apply

Submit a resume, cover letter and three professional references. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Equal Opportunity

Description

The Partnership Project is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization focused on supporting the collaborative efforts of the environmental community. Our programs focus on critical environmental issues including climate change, emissions reduction, and environmental and climate justice.

We provide fiscal sponsorship and organizational support to our programs, empowering them to undertake the vital work of preserving our planet. Guided by our core principles of Equity, Integrity, Service, and Innovation, we are committed to fostering a healthy environment - both within our workplace and in the broader world. Through these values, we strive to make a meaningful contribution to creating a sustainable and positive impact on our planet and an inclusive workplace where everyone can bring their full and authentic self to do this critical work.

United to End Polluter Handouts (UTEPH) is a national, coalition-driven campaign working at the intersection of climate, democracy, and economic justice. Led by a diverse alliance of consumer, tax, youth, climate, environmental justice, faith, cultural, and economic justice organizations, UTEPH’s mission is to end oil and gas subsidies at every level of government within the next decade. The campaign prioritizes building durable power, activating new partnerships across diverse movements, by addressing the social and economic impacts of oil and gas subsidies on communities, health, affordability and economic justice.

The United States sits at an inflection point. The oil and gas industry’s political and economic power is reshaping policy, weakening environmental protections, and driving decisions that worsen climate, public health, affordability, and democracy. Families are paying more for fuel, utilities, and everyday goods even as the industry secures record profits, outsized executive compensation, and continued public subsidies.

At the same time, climate, economic, and environmental justice movements are being forced onto the defensive, fighting to protect hard-won gains, stop new extraction and infrastructure, and defend the right to advocate. Public handouts to polluters offer a critical strategic opening: they expose a vulnerable and often hidden source of industry power, tap broad public frustration with corporate capture, and create opportunities to build durable, cross-movement power around accountability and the public good.

The Campaign Director will help turn this opening into sustained power by aligning partners, sharpening strategy, and driving campaigns that make polluter handouts increasingly difficult to sustain at the federal, state, and local levels. Over the next 2–3 years, this role will help translate complex tax and finance issues into compelling public narratives, coordinate cross-movement campaigns, and build the infrastructure needed to sustain momentum and drive results.

The coalition includes Center for Popular Democracy, Climate Democracy Initiative, Friends of the Earth, GoodPower, GreenFaith, Hip Hop Caucus, Oil Change International, Our Revolution, Public Citizen, Sierra Club, Sunrise Movement, Texas Campaign for the Environment Fund, The FACT Coalition, We Build Progress, and Zero Hour, among others.

Within this coalition context, the Campaign Director will provide the strategic leadership, coordination, and operational oversight needed to align partners and move the campaign forward.

Drive day-to-day campaign coordination to ensure strong communication, effective operations, and progress toward shared goals.

Build and maintain strong relationships with campaign partners, allies, and workgroups across research, advocacy, communications, organizing, and mobilization.
Convene and facilitate campaign calls, workgroups, and partner meetings to move action items, surface decisions, and maintain alignment.
Expand the coalition’s reach, diversity, and power.

Communications & Narrative

Oversee campaign communications and help align messaging, narrative, and communications strategy across coalition partners and external consultants.
Draft and/or review strategy documents, talking points, and public-facing communications as needed.

Fundraising, Budgeting & Operations

Oversee fundraising-related planning and coordination, including proposal development, grant reporting, and regranting to collaborative partners.
Oversee budget tracking, expense reporting, and financial coordination in partnership with the fiscal sponsor and campaign administrators.

Planning, Goals & Performance Tracking

Establish clear goals, benchmarks, and decision-making processes across workstreams.
Track progress, assess impact, and share regular updates with coalition partners and administrative managers.

Marginal Duties

Travel as needed to Washington, D.C., and states where UTEPH is building an active presence to support meetings, coalition building, working groups, events, etc.
Work occasional evenings and weekends to support UTEPH coalition events.

Requirements

Budget, Fundraising & Operations Experience

Critical Competencies

Initiative: Identifies opportunities and challenges and acts without waiting to be asked.

About Cushing Academy

Cushing Academy is a coeducational, college preparatory boarding and day school in Ashburnham, Massachusetts, serving students in grades 9–12 and post-graduate. Founded in 1865, Cushing Academy is guided by its mission to develop “curious, creative, and confident learners and leaders,” placing students at the center of a dynamic, supportive, and diverse community.

Cushing offers a rigorous and personalized academic experience, with small class sizes, a strong student-faculty ratio, and a wide range of programs across disciplines including STEM, visual and performing arts, and global studies. Dedicated faculty provide close mentorship and academic support, helping students build confidence, think critically, and prepare for success in college and beyond. Graduates attend a distinguished range of four-year colleges and universities, a reflection of Cushing’s rigorous college preparatory program and its focus on developing students who are prepared to excel beyond Cushing.

Life at Cushing extends well beyond the classroom, with robust opportunities in athletics, the arts, and student-led clubs and activities. Students participate in competitive sports teams, creative arts programs, and a wide array of organizations, from Model United Nations to a cappella, while also enjoying a vibrant residential life filled with campus events, leadership opportunities, and weekend excursions. This breadth of experiences, combined with a strong sense of community, empowers students to explore their passions, form lasting relationships, and thrive as engaged, well-rounded individuals.

Philanthropy plays a vital role in sustaining and advancing Cushing Academy’s mission, supporting both the immediate student experience and the school’s long-term priorities. Cushing fosters a strong culture of giving among alumni, parents, and friends, whose collective generosity ensures continued investment in academic programs, faculty excellence, financial aid, and student life. This shared commitment reflects a deep belief in the value of a Cushing education and its impact on students’ growth and success.

The Cushing Fund annual giving program provides flexible, unrestricted support for core operations. Additional philanthropic support strengthens the endowment and advances strategic initiatives, ensuring that Cushing can remain both innovative and accessible.

Cushing’s advancement program prioritizes meaningful, long-term engagement with its community through annual, major, and planned giving, as well as advancing an alumni engagement program with strong institutional support and growth potential. VoltaGrid is seeking an experienced Chief of Staff to serve as a trusted strategic and operational partner to the Chief Executive Officer. The Chief of Staff must be equally comfortable in the Boardroom, at a manufacturing facility, in the field, or meeting with customers, investors, and business partners. This is not an administrative role. It is an executive-level position focused on increasing the CEO’s effectiveness and ensuring that the company’s most important priorities are executed.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership to the CEO

Serve as a trusted adviser and thought partner to the CEO on business, operational, organizational, and strategic matters.
Help the CEO prioritize time and attention around the issues and opportunities that have the greatest impact on the company.
Translate the CEO’s direction into clear objectives, action plans, accountable owners, and measurable outcomes.
Anticipate issues requiring the CEO’s attention and ensure the CEO has the information needed to make timely, well-informed decisions.
Provide candid, objective counsel and help pressure-test important decisions, organizational changes, and strategic opportunities.
Represent the CEO in selected meetings and initiatives when appropriate.
Work closely with the CEO’s Executive Assistant to coordinate priorities, preparation, travel, meetings, and follow-through.

Travel With the CEO

Travel regularly with the CEO to VoltaGrid facilities, field locations, customer sites, Board meetings, investor meetings, industry events, and other business engagements.
Ensure the CEO is fully prepared for each engagement through concise briefing materials, relevant background information, key messages, anticipated questions, and clearly defined objectives.
Participate in meetings alongside the CEO, capture decisions, and commitments, and ensure appropriate follow-up.
Build relationships with employees, customers, investors, advisers, and business partners while representing the CEO and VoltaGrid professionally.
Use facility and field visits to identify operational challenges, organizational concerns, and opportunities that may not be visible at the corporate level.
Maintain flexibility to travel on short notice and accommodate business needs outside traditional working hours when necessary.
Travel is expected to be both planned and situational and may include frequent domestic travel and occasional international travel.

Strategy and Enterprise Execution

Help convert VoltaGrid’s strategic plan into a practical operating agenda for the executive leadership team.
Lead or coordinate high-priority initiatives that cross multiple functions or business units.
Establish clear ownership, timelines, milestones, and reporting for the company’s most important priorities.
Identify barriers to execution and work with executive leaders to resolve them quickly.
Develop analyses, recommendations, and executive-level materials to support major business decisions.
Track commitments made by the CEO and executive leadership team and ensure consistent follow-through.
Step into complex or time-sensitive projects when additional leadership, structure, or coordination is required.

Executive Leadership and Operating Rhythm

Establish and manage an effective operating cadence for the CEO and executive leadership team.
Coordinate executive meetings, operating reviews, strategic planning sessions, and leadership off-sites.
Ensure meetings are focused on decisions, accountability, risks, performance, and business outcomes.
Document important decisions, assign accountable owners, and monitor completion of agreed-upon actions.
Improve the quality and consistency of communication among the CEO, executive leadership team, Board, and broader organization.
Promote clear decision rights and accountability as VoltaGrid continues to scale.

Public-Company Readiness

Partner with Finance, Legal, People Operations, Communications, Operations, and external advisers on public-company-readiness initiatives.
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams involving governance, internal controls, reporting processes, risk management, organizational readiness, and executive communications.
Help establish the planning, documentation, and operating discipline expected of a public company.
Support the preparation of the company’s strategic narrative, key performance messages, and executive presentations.
Monitor readiness milestones, identify potential gaps, and escalate issues requiring executive attention.
Exercise exceptional discretion regarding confidential financial, legal, personnel, transaction, and investor-related information.

Board, Investor, and External Stakeholder Support

Partner with the CEO, CFO, General Counsel, and other leaders to prepare Board and committee materials.
Coordinate Board agendas, presentations, decision points, and follow-up actions.
Prepare the CEO for meetings with investors, lenders, customers, strategic partners, advisers, and other external stakeholders.
Help ensure that messaging is accurate, consistent, and aligned with VoltaGrid’s strategy and performance.
Support the development of Board- and investor-quality presentations that clearly communicate performance, opportunities, risks, and priorities.

Organizational Effectiveness and Culture

Build trusted relationships across the organization, from executive leadership to employees working in VoltaGrid’s facilities and field operations.
Serve as a connection point between the CEO and the broader organization while maintaining appropriate confidentiality.
Identify organizational friction, communication gaps, and emerging concerns before they become larger issues.
Reinforce a culture of accountability, urgency, safety, transparency, and operational excellence.
Help ensure that company-wide initiatives are understood and consistently implemented across locations.
Model VoltaGrid’s values and leadership expectations in every interaction.

Other Requirements

10 or more years of progressive experience in strategy, operations, finance, consulting, corporate development, investment banking, or a comparable leadership position.
Experience supporting a CEO, executive leadership team, Board of Directors, or similarly senior stakeholders.
Experience in energy, power generation, oil and gas, industrial services, manufacturing, infrastructure, or another operationally complex and asset-intensive business strongly preferred.
Experience in a high-growth, private-equity-backed, acquisitive, pre-IPO, or public-company environment is highly valued.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives involving multiple business units and senior leaders.
Strong financial and operational acumen, with the ability to understand business performance and translate data into actionable recommendations.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing executive-, Board-, or investor-level materials.
Strong judgment and the ability to handle sensitive information with complete discretion.
High emotional intelligence and the ability to influence others without relying on formal authority.
Ability to operate effectively in corporate, manufacturing, and field environments.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly with the CEO, sometimes on short notice.

Highly organized, responsive, and accountable.
Strategic enough to see the larger picture and operational enough to drive the details.
Comfortable working at a fast pace and making progress despite ambiguity.
Direct, confident, and capable of providing the CEO with honest feedback.

Yad Vashem USA Foundation is pleased to work with DRG to conduct this search.

BACKGROUND

About Yad Vashem

Yad Vashem’s mission is to lead the documentation, research, education, and commemoration of the Holocaust, and to convey the chronicles of this singular Jewish and human event to every person in Israel, to the Jewish people, and to every significant and relevant audience worldwide.

Yad Vashem serves as a global center for documentation, research, education, and commemoration, preserving the memory of six million Jews while confronting distortion, denial, and antisemitism. Housing the largest and most comprehensive collection of Holocaust artifacts, documents, photographs, and survivor testimonies, Yad Vashem ensures this history remains credible and accessible for future generations.

Beyond remembrance, Yad Vashem is a living institution with an urgent contemporary mission. As the world enters an era without living Holocaust survivors, the responsibility to convey the lessons of this singular human tragedy has never been greater. Through rigorous scholarship, innovative education, and global outreach, Yad Vashem engages diverse audiences and stands as a lasting beacon of historical truth, moral clarity, and human dignity.

About Yad Vashem USA Foundation

Yad Vashem USA Foundation (YVUSA) was established to support and advance Yad Vashem’s mission by deepening engagement and investment across the United States. Built from the ground up, YVUSA has exceeded initial fundraising goals and laid the foundation for long-term growth.

YVUSA operates with a small, highly committed national team and an engaged board, with a growing presence in New York, Florida, California, and other regions across the country. At its core, YVUSA is driven by a belief that supporting Yad Vashem is not only an act of remembrance, but a commitment to truth, education, and moral clarity in an increasingly complex world.

To learn more, please visit: https://yadvashemfoundation.org/

The Position

The Director of Development, California is a new and pivotal role for Yad Vashem USA Foundation (YVUSA). Joining at a time of significant growth and opportunity, the Director will build on the momentum already established in California while expanding YVUSA’s reach, visibility, and philanthropic support across the region.

Working in close collaboration with the national office, the Director will help shape and grow YVUSA’s presence in California, with a primary focus on Los Angeles and Southern California. The Director will build relationships with prospective donors and community leaders, engage existing supporters, and create opportunities for people across the region to connect with Yad Vashem and its mission. The role will also help establish the structure and relationships needed to build a strong and sustainable regional fundraising effort.

The role calls for someone who can think strategically while also being highly hands-on. The Director will develop and execute fundraising strategies, personally cultivate and solicit major donors, and create meaningful opportunities for donor engagement. Success will require close collaboration with national and volunteer leadership, as well as the ability to translate broader YVUSA priorities into effective work on the ground in Los Angeles and Southern California.

Reporting to Deputy National Director Beth Katznelson and working closely with National Director Tamar Major, the Director will be an important part of YVUSA’s expanding team. Over time, the Director will have the opportunity to help shape and lead a growing regional team as YVUSA continues to strengthen its presence in California.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Grow YVUSA’s presence in Los Angeles and Southern California by building on the momentum already underway and expanding the organization’s network of donors, prospects, and community leaders.
Build and manage a strong portfolio of prospects and donors, moving relationships from initial engagement through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, with a focus on five- and six-figure gifts and above.
Create a dynamic regional fundraising program through donor gatherings, parlor meetings, speaker programs, events, and other opportunities that bring people closer to Yad Vashem’s mission.
Develop and activate volunteer leadership, cultivating strong relationships with local board members and helping establish a regional advisory committee.
Serve as a visible representative of YVUSA and Yad Vashem, building awareness and engagement across Los Angeles and the broader Southern California Jewish and philanthropic communities.
Partner closely with national leadership to translate YVUSA’s broader fundraising priorities into a focused strategy for Los Angeles, Southern California, and, over time, the broader California market .

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate will be an entrepreneurial and accomplished fundraising professional who is excited by the opportunity to build a growing regional presence and expand YVUSA’s philanthropic support in the region.
Strong track record of success in major gifts fundraising, including five- and six-figure solicitations.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and public speaking skills, with the ability to build trust and engage donors and community leaders.
Collaborative and team-oriented, with the ability to work effectively with national staff, volunteer leaders, and colleagues across the organization.
Self-motivated, organized, and able to independently set priorities, manage a portfolio, and follow through.
Entrepreneurial and creative, with the ability to identify opportunities and build a fundraising program with initiative and resourcefulness.
Familiarity with the Los Angeles and Southern California Jewish communal and philanthropic landscape, with broader California experience a plus.
Passion for YVUSA’s mission and the ability to effectively communicate its importance to a range of audiences.
Ability to work evenings and weekends and travel regionally and to Israel as needed.
Salesforce experience preferred.

LOCATION AND WORK MODEL

This a remote role with a preference for candidates based in Los Angeles. The role requires regional travel throughout California and the west coast, periodic travel to New York, and occasional travel to Israel.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Yad Vashem USA Foundation offers a comprehensive and competitive compensation and benefits package for this role. The salary range for this position is $180,000–$200,000.

About OpenAI Foundation

AI is already changing how people work, learn, and access care. It has the potential to unlock extraordinary benefits—faster medical breakthroughs, accelerated scientific discovery, more personalized services in healthcare and education, new tools for creativity and invention, higher productivity and economic growth, improved public services like transportation systems, and so much more.

But building powerful systems to benefit humanity is only a part of the work of our mission. Advanced AI models will also present new challenges that are already surfacing, and we need to be prepared to identify these challenges and develop solutions to address them.

These are the two dimensions of what we’re building the Foundation to do. We aim to enable the use of AI to find solutions to humanity’s hardest problems, transform what people are capable of, and deliver real benefits in people’s lives—while working hard with partners to be ready for new challenges, and to help make society resilient, as AI advances.

This work is just beginning. Over the next year, as we quickly ramp up, the Foundation expects to invest at least $1 billion across life sciences and curing diseases, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs. This includes early investments toward our previously announced $25 billion commitment to curing diseases and AI resilience.

About Civil Society And Philanthropy

Civil Society and Philanthropy is a new OpenAI Foundation team dedicated to putting advanced AI to work on challenges facing people and communities globally.

We will partner with nonprofit and civil society organizations and governments around the world, putting in place the resources needed to ensure AI can meaningfully support their work. We combine philanthropic investment, technical expertise, and convening power to work alongside trusted partners that deliver essential services across geographies and issue areas. Together, we identify opportunities where AI can strengthen their work, expand their reach, and tangibly benefit their communities.

We're starting with three areas:

Put AI to work in essential services where it can meaningfully improve access and outcomes.
Give civil society organizations the tools, expertise, and support to adopt AI responsibly.
Build shared infrastructure so that successful tools and lessons can benefit the entire social sector.

We believe the most meaningful applications of AI will be shaped not by technology companies alone, but by the teachers, clinicians, legal advocates, public servants, researchers, governments, and community organizations applying these tools to solve real-world problems.

The Program Director is a leadership role on the Catalytic Deployments team that combines philanthropic investment, strategy, institution-building, and operations. Catalytic Deployments is a small, flat, and fast-moving team designed to make large and transformative investments across a wide range of areas in civil society.

Program Directors own the strategy and execution of major areas of the Catalytic Deployments portfolio, working closely with the Head of Catalytic Deployments to set overall team priorities. In the first year, Program Directors will develop a clear investment thesis in one or more priority domains; build a high-quality pipeline of opportunities; launch several significant partnerships or investments; and help establish the operating model and team for Catalytic Deployments.

This role reports to the Head of Catalytic Deployments, Civil Society and Philanthropy.

Credible experience building and scaling large social-sector initiatives
Experience in sourcing, assessing, and structuring grants

The Director of Strategic Partnerships will lead the strategy, growth, and performance of Circle's partnerships function, building programs and relationships that strengthen Circle's brand while driving meaningful business outcomes.

You'll be responsible for translating Circle's broader company priorities into a forward-looking partnerships strategy, identifying where and how we invest, developing our most important creator and strategic relationships, and ensuring those investments translate into measurable impact across customer growth, brand awareness, and market position.

Own Circle's Partnerships strategic planning, and roadmap, using deep, company-wide knowledge of Circle's business, strategy, and goals to originate new concepts and ideas that extend the function's impact beyond its current scope — connecting partnership investments to company priorities, measurable business outcomes, and providing strategic direction to managers across multiple areas and operations.
Take ownership of the function's contribution to new business and other agreed performance goals, using those outcomes to inform where we invest, what we build, and how we prioritize.
Build repeatable partnership programs and playbooks that allow successful initiatives such as webinars, challenges, creator campaigns, launches, and event activations to scale without requiring the same level of hands-on involvement each time.

Lead Circle's highest-value creator and strategic partnerships, including relationship development, opportunity identification, deal strategy, negotiation, creative direction, and long-term growth.
Shape the content and creative strategy behind major partnerships, working closely with partners to develop ideas that are authentic to their audience, differentiated in the market, and effective for Circle. Bring a strong marketing mindset into partnership development, including offer strategy, audience journeys, conversion opportunities, and ways Circle and its partners can create greater value together over time.

Establish clear measurement, reporting, and decision-making frameworks for the function, using performance and qualitative insights to improve future investments.
Support cross-functional teams in a consultative capacity on any content-forward initiatives.

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English (CEFR C2 or equivalent), as most collaboration at Circle happens asynchronously.
10+ years of experience building 6-7 figure strategic partnerships, creator programs, brand initiatives, or strategic growth programs within SaaS, technology, the creator economy, or a similarly fast-moving industry.
Strong business development skills including pipeline management, negotiation, partner development, and cross-functional project management.
Performance marketing instincts and an understanding of how partnerships can drive both brand value and measurable business outcomes.
Deep understanding of Circle's customers, the creator economy, and the broader market, with a point of view on where Circle can build differentiated relationships and influence.
Experience developing and growing high-value relationships, with strong judgment around deal structure, negotiation, partner dynamics, and long-term opportunity.

About INSPIRE Alliance

INSPIRE Alliance is a Texas nonprofit corporation established by the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station (TEES) with support from The Texas A&M University System Board of Regents. The Alliance was created to advance leadership in applied national security research by accelerating the development and deployment of mission-ready engineering solutions.

As a 501(c)(3) organization, INSPIRE Alliance provides a flexible platform for pursuing contracts, grants and strategic partnerships in the national security sector. Working across government, academia and industry, the Alliance is designed to rapidly translate research and innovation into real-world capabilities that strengthen security, resilience and operational effectiveness.

INSPIRE Alliance focuses on critical technology areas including autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, space innovation, data science and advanced materials. Its mission is to serve as a trusted agent for engineering solutions while expanding research impact, strengthening strategic partnerships and advancing national security priorities.

Position Summary

INSPIRE Alliance is seeking a President & Chief Executive Officer to serve as the organization's principal executive leader and guide its next phase of development and growth.

The CEO will be responsible for transforming an emerging organizational platform into a mature, high-performing national security research and innovation enterprise. This executive will establish the strategic direction, operating capability, sponsor relationships, talent and infrastructure necessary to scale the Alliance while preserving the speed, flexibility and mission focus that distinguish its operating model.

Operating at the intersection of national security, federal contracting, institutional governance and academic research, the CEO must be equally credible in defense and university environments. The successful candidate will understand the urgency and acquisition priorities of federal sponsors while effectively navigating the governance, research and administrative structures of a university-affiliated organization.

Working closely with the Board of Directors and executive leadership, the CEO will position INSPIRE Alliance as a premier partner for federal agencies, military organizations, academic institutions and industry seeking mission-ready research, engineering and technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, Growth and Organizational Scale
Establish and execute a long-term strategic vision aligned with the INSPIRE Alliance mission, Department of War priorities and national security objectives.
Build the organizational capabilities required to scale from an emerging enterprise into a mature, sustainable and high-output operating organization.
Translate strategic priorities into measurable goals, performance indicators and accountable execution plans.
Identify opportunities for program expansion, new capabilities and strategic investment while maintaining disciplined focus on mission impact.
Sustain a high-energy, project-driven operating culture that values speed, sound judgment and execution without sacrificing quality or compliance.

Federal Growth and Sponsor Development
Develop and expand relationships with senior leaders across the Department of War, military services, federal agencies, service laboratories, program executive offices (PEOs) and other national security organizations.
Position INSPIRE Alliance for competitive federal opportunities, including prime contract roles, strategic teaming arrangements and consortium-based partnerships.
Apply strong knowledge of federal acquisition and contracting pathways, including Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) vehicles and Other Transaction Authority/Agreement (OTA) mechanisms.
Lead organizational revenue growth through federal contracts, grants, sponsorships, partnerships and other diversified funding sources in coordination with the Director of Business Development.
Build sustained sponsor relationships by understanding mission requirements, anticipating emerging priorities and ensuring INSPIRE Alliance delivers measurable value.

Organizational Leadership and Operations
Provide executive oversight of programs, finance, compliance, human capital, infrastructure and organizational administration.
Recruit, develop and retain high-performing leaders and teams capable of operating effectively in a complex national security environment.
Establish scalable business processes, management systems and secure operating practices that support growth across a substantial sponsored portfolio.
Monitor organizational performance, resolve barriers to execution and continuously strengthen operational effectiveness.
Foster a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, integrity and disciplined decision-making.

Governance, Financial Stewardship and Risk
Serve as the principal executive liaison to the Board of Directors, providing timely, transparent and strategic information necessary for effective governance and decision-making.
Execute Board-approved policies, initiatives and organizational priorities.
Maintain strong financial stewardship through disciplined budgeting, resource allocation, forecasting and executive-level financial reporting.
Establish and maintain effective governance, compliance and enterprise risk management practices appropriate for a national security-focused nonprofit organization.
Ensure disciplined management of security-sensitive requirements, including ITAR, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements and classified information handling as applicable.
Exercise sound executive judgment in evaluating opportunities, including declining work when compliance, security or institutional risk outweighs strategic value.

External Leadership and Strategic Partnerships
Serve as the principal ambassador for INSPIRE Alliance with government, military, university, industry and community stakeholders.
Build productive relationships across The Texas A&M University System, faculty, research leadership and academic administration while protecting the Alliance's ability to operate with appropriate speed and flexibility.
Communicate effectively with senior military leaders, government executives, industry partners, researchers and institutional leaders, translating priorities across defense and academic environments.
Strengthen collaboration among academia, government and industry to accelerate the transition of research and technology into operational capability.
Represent INSPIRE Alliance at executive meetings, industry forums, sponsor engagements and other external events.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business administration, public policy, higher education, nonprofit management or a related field.
Master's degree in business administration, public administration, organizational leadership or a related field.
Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience in national security, nonprofit leadership, higher education, applied research, research alliances or another mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated success building or scaling organizations, programs or business units through significant periods of growth and increasing operational complexity.
Proven record of developing federal sponsor relationships and securing substantial funding through contracts, grants, partnerships, sponsorships or other revenue sources.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across government, academia and industry, including the ability to reconcile differing institutional cultures, priorities and decision-making processes.
Strong understanding of federal acquisition, contracting and sponsored research environments.
Executive-level financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation and Board-level financial reporting.
Experience establishing effective governance, compliance, security and risk management practices.
Demonstrated success leading senior teams and developing high-performing organizations.
Exceptional executive communication, relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to make sound decisions in complex, ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.
Demonstrated integrity, discretion and sound judgment in matters involving sensitive information, institutional risk and public trust.
Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Significant experience supporting Department of War programs, federal contracts, military acquisition organizations or national security initiatives.
Established relationships across federal defense organizations, military services, program executive offices, laboratories or related sponsor communities.
Experience leading a university-affiliated applied research organization, national security nonprofit, federal research enterprise, defense-focused business or similar organization.

Prior military service, particularly experience as a commissioned officer, commander or acquisition leader.

Executive Leadership Profile

The successful CEO will be a builder rather than a caretaker. INSPIRE Alliance requires an executive capable of strengthening the organization's operating foundation while aggressively pursuing the relationships, capabilities and opportunities necessary for long-term scale.

This leader must be fluent in both the language of national security and the culture of academic research. The CEO must understand mission capability, sponsor urgency and acquisition priorities while maintaining credibility with faculty, researchers and university leadership.

Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and thrive in a complex environment with multiple priorities.

Develop and lead implementation of Art with a Heart’s annual fundraising strategy, including goals, revenue projections, strategies, timelines, and metrics across individual, foundation, and corporate donations.

Description

The Partnership Project is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization focused on supporting the collaborative efforts of the environmental community. Our programs focus on critical environmental issues including climate change, emissions reduction, and environmental and climate justice.

We provide fiscal sponsorship and organizational support to our programs, empowering them to undertake the vital work of preserving our planet. Guided by our core principles of Equity, Integrity, Service, and Innovation, we are committed to fostering a healthy environment - both within our workplace and in the broader world. Through these values, we strive to make a meaningful contribution to creating a sustainable and positive impact on our planet and an inclusive workplace where everyone can bring their full and authentic self to do this critical work.

United to End Polluter Handouts (UTEPH) is a national, coalition-driven campaign working at the intersection of climate, democracy, and economic justice. Led by a diverse alliance of consumer, tax, youth, climate, environmental justice, faith, cultural, and economic justice organizations, UTEPH’s mission is to end oil and gas subsidies at every level of government within the next decade. The campaign prioritizes building durable power, activating new partnerships across diverse movements, by addressing the social and economic impacts of oil and gas subsidies on communities, health, affordability and economic justice.

The United States sits at an inflection point. The oil and gas industry’s political and economic power is reshaping policy, weakening environmental protections, and driving decisions that worsen climate, public health, affordability, and democracy. Families are paying more for fuel, utilities, and everyday goods even as the industry secures record profits, outsized executive compensation, and continued public subsidies.

At the same time, climate, economic, and environmental justice movements are being forced onto the defensive, fighting to protect hard-won gains, stop new extraction and infrastructure, and defend the right to advocate. Public handouts to polluters offer a critical strategic opening: they expose a vulnerable and often hidden source of industry power, tap broad public frustration with corporate capture, and create opportunities to build durable, cross-movement power around accountability and the public good.

The Campaign Director will help turn this opening into sustained power by aligning partners, sharpening strategy, and driving campaigns that make polluter handouts increasingly difficult to sustain at the federal, state, and local levels. Over the next 2–3 years, this role will help translate complex tax and finance issues into compelling public narratives, coordinate cross-movement campaigns, and build the infrastructure needed to sustain momentum and drive results.

The coalition includes Center for Popular Democracy, Climate Democracy Initiative, Friends of the Earth, GoodPower, GreenFaith, Hip Hop Caucus, Oil Change International, Our Revolution, Public Citizen, Sierra Club, Sunrise Movement, Texas Campaign for the Environment Fund, The FACT Coalition, We Build Progress, and Zero Hour, among others.

Within this coalition context, the Campaign Director will provide the strategic leadership, coordination, and operational oversight needed to align partners and move the campaign forward.

Expand the coalition’s reach, diversity, and power.

Communications & Narrative

Draft and/or review strategy documents, talking points, and public-facing communications as needed.

Fundraising, Budgeting & Operations

Establish clear goals, benchmarks, and decision-making processes across workstreams.
Track progress, assess impact, and share regular updates with coalition partners and administrative managers.

Marginal Duties

Cushing Academy is a coeducational, college preparatory boarding and day school in Ashburnham, Massachusetts, serving students in grades 9–12 and post-graduate. Founded in 1865, Cushing Academy is guided by its mission to develop “curious, creative, and confident learners and leaders,” placing students at the center of a dynamic, supportive, and diverse community.

Cushing offers a rigorous and personalized academic experience, with small class sizes, a strong student-faculty ratio, and a wide range of programs across disciplines including STEM, visual and performing arts, and global studies. Dedicated faculty provide close mentorship and academic support, helping students build confidence, think critically, and prepare for success in college and beyond. Graduates attend a distinguished range of four-year colleges and universities, a reflection of Cushing’s rigorous college preparatory program and its focus on developing students who are prepared to excel beyond Cushing.

Life at Cushing extends well beyond the classroom, with robust opportunities in athletics, the arts, and student-led clubs and activities. Students participate in competitive sports teams, creative arts programs, and a wide array of organizations, from Model United Nations to a cappella, while also enjoying a vibrant residential life filled with campus events, leadership opportunities, and weekend excursions. This breadth of experiences, combined with a strong sense of community, empowers students to explore their passions, form lasting relationships, and thrive as engaged, well-rounded individuals.

Philanthropy plays a vital role in sustaining and advancing Cushing Academy’s mission, supporting both the immediate student experience and the school’s long-term priorities. This shared commitment reflects a deep belief in the value of a Cushing education and its impact on students’ growth and success.

The Cushing Fund annual giving program provides flexible, unrestricted support for core operations. Contributions to The Cushing Fund help bridge the gap between tuition and the full cost of educating each student, enabling enhancements across classrooms, co-curricular offerings, and residential life. Additional philanthropic support strengthens the endowment and advances strategic initiatives, ensuring that Cushing can remain both innovative and accessible.

Cushing’s advancement program prioritizes meaningful, long-term engagement with its community through annual, major, and planned giving, as well as advancing an alumni engagement program with strong institutional support and growth potential. BACKGROUND

About Yad Vashem

Yad Vashem’s mission is to lead the documentation, research, education, and commemoration of the Holocaust, and to convey the chronicles of this singular Jewish and human event to every person in Israel, to the Jewish people, and to every significant and relevant audience worldwide.

Yad Vashem serves as a global center for documentation, research, education, and commemoration, preserving the memory of six million Jews while confronting distortion, denial, and antisemitism. Housing the largest and most comprehensive collection of Holocaust artifacts, documents, photographs, and survivor testimonies, Yad Vashem ensures this history remains credible and accessible for future generations.

Beyond remembrance, Yad Vashem is a living institution with an urgent contemporary mission. As the world enters an era without living Holocaust survivors, the responsibility to convey the lessons of this singular human tragedy has never been greater. Through rigorous scholarship, innovative education, and global outreach, Yad Vashem engages diverse audiences and stands as a lasting beacon of historical truth, moral clarity, and human dignity.

About Yad Vashem USA Foundation

Yad Vashem USA Foundation (YVUSA) was established to support and advance Yad Vashem’s mission by deepening engagement and investment across the United States. Built from the ground up, YVUSA has exceeded initial fundraising goals and laid the foundation for long-term growth.

YVUSA operates with a small, highly committed national team and an engaged board, with a growing presence in New York, Florida, California, and other regions across the country. At its core, YVUSA is driven by a belief that supporting Yad Vashem is not only an act of remembrance, but a commitment to truth, education, and moral clarity in an increasingly complex world.

To learn more, please visit: https://yadvashemfoundation.org/

The Position

The Director of Development, California is a new and pivotal role for Yad Vashem USA Foundation (YVUSA). Joining at a time of significant growth and opportunity, the Director will build on the momentum already established in California while expanding YVUSA’s reach, visibility, and philanthropic support across the region.

BACKGROUND

About Yad Vashem

Yad Vashem’s mission is to lead the documentation, research, education, and commemoration of the Holocaust, and to convey the chronicles of this singular Jewish and human event to every person in Israel, to the Jewish people, and to every significant and relevant audience worldwide.

Yad Vashem serves as a global center for documentation, research, education, and commemoration, preserving the memory of six million Jews while confronting distortion, denial, and antisemitism. Housing the largest and most comprehensive collection of Holocaust artifacts, documents, photographs, and survivor testimonies, Yad Vashem ensures this history remains credible and accessible for future generations.

Beyond remembrance, Yad Vashem is a living institution with an urgent contemporary mission. As the world enters an era without living Holocaust survivors, the responsibility to convey the lessons of this singular human tragedy has never been greater. Through rigorous scholarship, innovative education, and global outreach, Yad Vashem engages diverse audiences and stands as a lasting beacon of historical truth, moral clarity, and human dignity.
